item.title: The Value of U.S. Land Power
item.description: Drones, AI, and long-range fires are reshaping warfare, but land power remains vital to achieving political and strategic objectives. CSIS’s Future of Land Power study examines why ground forces endure—and how they must adapt for future conflict as part of the joint force.

item.title: Are SBIR “Mills” Truly a Problem?
item.description: The Small Business Innovation Research Program has faced suggestions that a small number of “mills” receive a disproportionate share of awards while underperforming on innovation and commercialization metrics. An analysis of grant recipient data suggests this pattern reflects a division between specialized defense research contractors and dual-use venture-backed companies.

item.title: The Implications of Japan’s New National Intelligence Bureau
item.description: Japan’s new National Intelligence Bureau is an important early step in Japanese intelligence reform and creates opportunities for deeper cooperation with the United States and other partners.

item.title: The Cyberattacks on the U.S Water Sector and the Iran Question: Escalation or Opportunism?
item.description: It is highly likely that Iran is behind the cyberattacks on the U.S. water sector. Psychological effect—not escalation—is the point of Iran’s cyber operations, to sow fear, chaos, and division as part of its information warfare strategy.

item.title: Is a New Chinese Runway Taking Flight at Antelope Reef?
item.description: China begins construction at Antelope Reef.

item.title: After Iran: A Scenario for Renewed Trump-Kim Summitry
item.description: The conventional policy wisdom is that President Trump’s enthusiasm for reengagement is not shared by Kim Jong-un. But Victor Cha argues that a unique set of drivers, including North Korean revisionism, could spur a renewal of diplomacy.

item.title: The Houthis Enter the Iran War and Everything Gets Worse
item.description: The Houthis’ entry into the Iran war is creating a dangerous new front for Saudi Arabia—potentially forcing it into a military escalation that the United States wants to avoid.

item.title: More Than Entertainment: Japan’s Creative Industries and the U.S.-Japan Partnership
item.description: As creative industries increasingly become a strategic pillar of economic competitiveness and geopolitical influence, Japan and the United States can leverage their complementary strengths to expand their global reach, deepen ties, and shape the information environment.

item.title: PacTech Pulse: August 2026
item.description: This edition of PacTech Pulse covers August 2026.

item.title: Government Lending 2.0: Putting a Price on Policy Risk
item.description: As federal credit becomes increasingly utilized, federal agencies need a framework to quantify policy risk and create a common language to balance strategic priorities with financial risks.
